text:
maya.sec: Quick advisory: starting 2026-08-01 we'll enforce a 90-day TTL on all service account keys and app secrets. Keys older than 90 days will be disabled and flagged for deletion. Goal: reduce long-lived credential risk. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/credential-ttl :warning:

infra-bot: scan results: 94 SA keys >90d, 27 app secrets >90d, 11 orphaned keys. Top services: analytics-batch, data-migration, internal-monitor. Full: https://redwood.internal/reports/ttl-scan-2105554321

sam.platform: will Dedicated/private customers be notified?

maya.sec: Yes. We will send notices to on-prem contacts and post guidance; auto-disable only applies to hosted control plane. Private customers get guidance and a remediation package.

ishaan.sre: impact on rolling jobs? need a short grace period for critical pipelines.

maya.sec: We have a 7-day grace window after disable where owners can request immediate rotate/restore via ticket `sec-urgent-cred`. Exceptions limited and logged. Please add owner metadata for any long-lived keys to avoid surprises.

deploy-bot: owners CSV export queued; DMing team leads for top-50 risky keys in 10m. Command: `curl -sS https://api.redwood.internal/infra/credentials?filter=old&format=csv -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"`

sam.platform: we'll run a migration sprint next week. Can security provide a small helper script for rotating GCP/Azure/AWS creds?

maya.sec: yes, small scripts and examples are in the runbook (GCP: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys create`, Azure: `az ad app credential reset`, AWS: `aws iam create-access-key`). If you need hands-on help, open a `sec-automations` ticket.

ishaan.sre: noted, scheduling maintenance.

maya.sec: TL;DR checklist:
- Owners: rotate keys >90d or add owner metadata by 2026-07-15.
- Security: final scan 2026-07-20, auto-disable 2026-08-01.
- Questions: sec-automations@redwood.com or ping me. :white_check_mark:
